transcript.text: Bosch HBS534BS0B oven displaying E011 and won't let me do anything. Beeping. Help!

E011 on Bosch ovens typically indicates a fault with the control system—either a stuck button on the panel or an internal communication error within the main PCB (the 'brain' of the oven). Because the oven is locked and beeping, we need to see if this is a temporary glitch or a hardware failure. Please try this safe reset:
1. Switch off the oven at the wall isolator switch or remove the relevant fuse from your consumer unit.
2. Wait for 2 minutes (this allows the electronics to fully discharge).
3. Switch it back on and see if the error clears. Let me know exactly what happens when you turn it back on.
Switched it off at the cooker switch for 5 minutes, then back on. It's come up normally with no code now. Clock's showing and it's accepting input again.

That is excellent news. It sounds like the control board had a temporary glitch or communication error that was cleared by the power reset. To help prevent this from happening again, try to avoid switching the oven off at the wall isolator unless there is an emergency; simply turning it off via the controls and leaving it on standby (or just using the timer) keeps the electronics happy. If you do need to cut the mains for a while, make sure to set the clock back to MANUAL mode when you turn it back on. Is there anything else I can help you with regarding your oven?

candidates: Control board / PCB fault or communication error (high)

reading.symptom: displaying error code, won't let me do anything, beeping

plan: Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Bosch; model HBS534BS0B; code E011.
The fault they reported is: "displaying error code, won't let me do anything, beeping". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.
The customer says it is fixed: say so warmly, give one short tip to stop it happening again, and ask if there is anything else.

facts.value: switched off at cooker switch for 5 minutes then back on: came up normally with no code, clock showing, accepting input
